basis: Anencephaly defines CNS involvement; cleft palate and anophthalmia each reported in 1/2 assessed patients; estimates rest on a very small cohort.
Intestinal epithelial disease; frequent renal findings and developmental delay do not establish direct damage independent of dehydration, malnutrition or parenteral nutrition.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction with chronic rhinitis and sinusitis in 4/4; situs inversus alone is not damage; cardiac malformations individually reported in <30%.
Nonsyndromic congenital digit and skeletal malformations; cutaneous syndactyly does not establish a separate skin disorder.
Malignant smooth muscle tumour arising in the inferior vena cava; vascular origin determines the axis.
Malignancy of foreskin, explicitly classified as skin cancer; its cutaneous origin supplies an axis despite the genital location.
Miliaria is a cutaneous sweat duct obstruction disorder.
SPEN-related neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability in 33/33; hypotonia accompanies neurological dysfunction; other damaging organ manifestations lack common frequencies.
Carcinoma arising in the ectocervix; reproductive organ malignancy has no axis. An infectious mechanism is not established by this concept.
Amino acid transport defect; developmental delay 10/10, osteoporosis 5/6, renal dysfunction 30-79%; frequent pulmonary, hepatic and blood damage omitted at the four-axis cap.
Umbrella of inherited carbohydrate transport and absorption defects; neurological, intestinal and other organ manifestations vary substantially by subtype.
Congenital neuromuscular junction disorder; weakness and ptosis reflect impaired transmission, not independent muscle or eye damage; endocrine involvement has no frequency.
Defined as infection of the external ear perichondrium and cartilage.
Congenital absence of olfactory bulbs and tracts causes anosmia; smell belongs to the neurological axis.
Malignancy of uterine adnexal structures, including broad and round ligaments; these reproductive structures are outside the locomotor connective tissue axis.
Defined by congenital heart disease, especially patent ductus arteriosus; additional syndromic features do not apply to most patients across the spectrum.
Developmental disability and skeletal/digital anomalies define the syndrome; hearing impairment 4/13 (~31%) narrowly supports ear involvement; isolated strabismus report is insufficient.
Broad hereditary nervous system disease category; muscle and other organ involvement is subtype-dependent.
Inherited cardiac electrical disorder causing arrhythmias and conduction abnormalities; syncope does not establish neurological damage.
Muscular dystrophy; cardiac conduction defects and cataracts each 80-99%, cognitive impairment 30-79%; supplied hypogonadism frequency is <30%.
Inherited immune dysregulation; autoimmune blood-cell destruction in 2/2 supports blood involvement; bronchiectasis in 1/1 is a separately diagnosed infectious complication.
Hereditary cerebellar ataxia; no evidence of common direct damage outside the nervous system.
Malignancy originating in the gastric pylorus.
Occlusion of a cerebral artery defines vascular disease; cerebral infarction is a separate consequence and is not established by this concept.
Combined congenital duodenal obstruction and tetralogy of Fallot directly define intestinal and cardiac involvement.
